key_insight: An AI-accelerated bottom-up simulation of living polymerization can resolve the amorphous microstructure of poly(1,3-dioxolane) by separating chain- and monomer-driven diffraction features across chain length.
engineering_relevance: This enables predictive, atomistic structure modeling for recyclable ultrahigh-molecular-weight polymers, supporting design and validation of materials with improved mechanical performance.
method: Reactive machine-learning force fields trained to vdW-corrected hybrid DFT
Simulated living cationic ring-opening polymerization under experimental conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports chain-length-resolved predictions that partition X-ray and neutron diffraction into a monomer peak near q≈1.5 Å^-1 and a polymer peak near q≈1.6 Å^-1, providing a direct target for experimental validation.
watch_item: Because the microstructure is inferred from simulations and ML force fields, the predictions depend on transferability of the trained potential and faithful matching of synthetic conditions to experiment.
paper_title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields
